title: Plan AR: AI Academic Writing
summary: Topic → literature search → outline → draft → de-duplicate & polish → submit
scenario: For students and researchers using AI as a writing and search aid, with strict academic integrity — AI assists, it never writes or thinks for you.

steps.title: Choose a topic
steps.detail: Brainstorm with the model: from your area of interest, have AI list research gaps, feasibility and material availability. Write the research question in one sentence — problem → method → contribution — and let the model stress-test whether it's too narrow or too broad.
steps.tips: Ask the model for 5 likely reviewer questions on this topic to expose defense or review risk early.

steps.title: Literature search
steps.detail: Use Perplexity for an initial scan, then read highly-cited and recent papers in detail on CNKI or Google Scholar. Build a literature table (authors, year, method, findings, your notes). Verify key data against original sources — AI invents references.
steps.tips: Require source links from Perplexity and click through; delete anything that won't open or can't be found.

steps.title: Outline
steps.detail: Build the outline to the target journal's structure: introduction → literature review → methods → results → discussion → conclusion, each section stating the core claim and supporting material. Have the model check the logical chain and fill any gaps.
steps.tips: Run the outline past your advisor or a peer before writing further — a wrong direction means rework no matter how much you write.

steps.title: Draft
steps.detail: Write section by section: methods first, then results (most objective), then introduction and literature review, discussion last. Feed your own material, data and rough paragraphs to the model to expand or rephrase — you judge and correct.
steps.tips: Never let AI write your core arguments wholesale; have it fill blanks inside your materials and framework so the author stays you.

steps.title: De-duplicate & polish
steps.detail: Run a similarity check first; for high-overlap paragraphs, have AI rewrite sentence structures and word choice, then use Grammarly for grammar and academic tone. Read the whole paper after to confirm meaning survived the rewrites.
steps.tips: After de-duplication, ask the model 'did the core claim of this paragraph change?' so you don't lose meaning to similarity.

steps.title: Submit
steps.detail: Use the model to draft the cover letter, author contributions and submission checklist, then verify against the target journal's formatting requirements item by item. Before submitting, have AI run a final self-check: figure numbering, citation format, headers, author info.
steps.tips: Have the model check each item against a 'submission checklist' and compare against it literally rather than by feel.

pitfalls.title: Submitting AI-written text directly
pitfalls.detail: That's the academic integrity line — AI-generated content passed off as original can constitute misconduct; AI does search, expansion and polishing, but the core ideas and data must be yours.

pitfalls.title: Citing hallucinated references
pitfalls.detail: Models invent non-existent papers and wrong volume/issue numbers; verify every citation against a database — better to omit than to fabricate.

pitfalls.title: Losing authorship to wholesale generation
pitfalls.detail: If the core argument isn't yours, a defense or reviewer question exposes it instantly; let AI work inside your framework and material while you own the conclusions.

pitfalls.title: Skipping advisor/peer review
pitfalls.detail: AI can't supply real disciplinary judgment; have an advisor or peer read the full draft before you submit and fix major issues first.
